claims.text: A nanoscale WS2 coating will reduce the coefficient of friction of the high-entropy alloy across a wide service-temperature range.
A nanoscale WS2 coating will reduce the wear rate of the high-entropy alloy across a wide service-temperature range.
WS2 is sufficiently stable for high-temperature service in the proposed application.
PVD can produce a uniform nanoscale WS2 coating on the alloy surface.
The coating should remain effective from near-ambient temperature to high service temperatures if adhesion and phase stability are maintained.
Sliding will produce a stable, lubricious WS2 tribolayer at the contact interface.
The WS2 tribolayer will act as a solid lubricant and protect the alloy substrate.
The WS2 tribolayer will have low shear strength.
The tribolayer will reduce direct asperity contact.
Reduced asperity contact will suppress abrasive wear.
Chemical and structural stability of WS2 at elevated temperatures will preserve lubrication over the entire service range.
The coating is predicted to reduce coefficient of friction by approximately 20–30% relative to the untreated alloy.
The coating is predicted to reduce wear rate by approximately 40–50% relative to the untreated alloy.
The untreated alloy has higher friction because of direct metal-to-metal contact.
Direct metal-to-metal contact and oxidation accelerate wear in the untreated alloy under operational conditions.
Coating integrity and adhesion under repeated loading and thermal cycling are necessary for the benefit to persist.
Coating degradation or delamination may eliminate the friction and wear improvements.
Performance under extreme or prolonged thermal cycling has not been fully characterized.
